items.html:
Both requested revisions were confirmed as clean HEADs: treams-rs fcf62400700e326ffcc61ec50025cb25ea43ea6d on release/integration; Advect d5f4bae154f040f1e80c32dc7c1aab41e4c155dc on main. All treams source below was read with git show at the pinned SHA.

Conclusion: Advect can be selected transparently from traced arguments and the existing Rust derivative adapter reused. The difficult part is preserving a coherent physics-object backend when some constructors receive only constants. A tracer detector alone does not solve that.

Source-confirmed findings:

  • Advect has a public detector: advect.is_traced(value) checks a tracer without reading its value. It is deliberately shallow: is_traced([tracer]) is false. The public export avoids depending on the concrete private tracer class. See Advect _array.py:14, public export at __init__.py:30.
  • Array namespace does not identify the autodiff owner. Advect’s NumPy tracer returns the underlying NumPy namespace from __array_namespace__; choosing NumPy from that answer would miss Advect. See _traced_array.py:328.
  • Ordinary NumPy composition is supported through protocols: tracer __array_ufunc__ and __array_function__ route supported operations through Advect, at _traced_array.py:549 and :577. This covers an expression such as np.sum(np.sin(x)**2); it does not register treams Rust operations or their derivatives.
  • Accidental coercion is not safe: current Advect np.asarray(tracer) raises TracingError at _traced_array.py:395. advect.asarray preserves direct tracers and rectangular nested tracer lists/tuples, at _array.py:132. Outside tracing it commonly returns ordinary NumPy arrays; therefore it does not tag an ordinary constant as “Advect.”
  • The derivative boundary already exists: treams_rs/advect.py:72 defines an @ad.primitive(..., residual=True) whose forward retains the Rust pullback and whose transpose invokes it. advect.py:108 normalizes dynamic arguments with ad.numpy.asarray before that primitive. Transparent dispatch should select this adapter, not try to make raw native calls traceable.
  • Shared constructors already make reuse practical: advect.py:1315 binds one Backend(ad.numpy, _operation) to _framework.Constructors and _framework.Operations. It exports physics constructors, shared physics classes, and numerous expert wrappers. These include sphere_tmatrix, plane_wave, slab, sphere, bessel, solve, and interaction.
  • Materials must be handled before scalar conversion: the ordinary Material calls complex() on all three values at _material.py:41. Framework Material simply retains epsilon, mu, and kappa, at _framework_backend.py:45. Supported dispatch must inspect material fields and known material tuples before invoking the ordinary constructor.
  • Constants are the central compositional issue: shared TMatrix stores its backend at _framework_tmatrix.py:59, while operations require both physics objects to have the same backend at _framework_backend.py:383. A proposed radius-only objective would dispatch sphere_tmatrix(radius=tracer, ...) to Advect but plane_wave(..., k0=1.3) to NumPy. The current shared implementation does not supply transparent promotion of that ordinary object.
  • Trace-context detection should not be the foundation: Advect has private core._context.is_tracing, but it is not exported from advect or advect.core. It reports both dynamic and staging traces (_context.py:307); detecting “some trace” would not establish that the treams adapter supports it. Public transform_state is bookkeeping for a dynamic transform, not a backend-selection API.

Advect limits and cotangents:

  • Existing treams adapter is CPU, first-order reverse mode only. jvp, nested differentiation, staging, and checkpointing are unsupported. See advect.py:1 and existing rejection tests test_advect.py:149.
  • These limits follow actual primitive definitions: there is a transpose, no JVP or abstract rule, and an opaque residual. Advect rejects nested residual use at _primitive_call.py:527 and checkpointed residuals at _primitive.py:382.
  • Advect and the native code use dL = Re(vdot(gradient, dx)); no cotangent conjugation is inserted. Gradients are cast back to each input’s dtype and shape, projecting real inputs to real gradients. Advect allows same-size scalar reshaping. See advect.py:92, _records.py:99.
  • The forward residual is consumed once; existing test uses vjp, calls the pullback twice, and expects the second call to raise “consumed” at test_advect.py:56.
  • Inputs can be float32/complex64 or double precision; Rust outputs are float64/complex128. Shared object Backend.apply verifies output shape and real/complex declaration, with one output per shared physics record (_framework_backend.py:314).

Suggested minimum policy, as inference:

  1. Dispatch only selected ordinary physics factories and supported object operations, using known continuous parameters, known material fields, and list/tuple containers. Reject mixed autodiff owners. Keep scalar/NumPy-only calls on the existing ordinary path.
  2. Use the receiver’s stored backend for methods and existing framework objects. Do not convert first and detect afterward.
  3. Give constant-only constructions one explicit backend choice, or deliberately implement narrowly defined ordinary-object promotion. The former is smaller. Avoid relying on global “currently tracing” state.
  4. Start with factories rather than claiming direct class constructors, every special function, every raw NumPy call, and all native symbols become transparent together.
  5. Lazy loading can consult an already imported Advect module and use its public is_traced predicate; then import treams_rs.advect only when selected. No backend registry is needed for three supported adapters. Inference: ordinary NumPy fast-path checks should not import optional dependencies or recursively traverse arbitrary object graphs.

Existing documented equivalent, runnable when treams-rs and its Advect extra are installed:

import advect as ad
import numpy as np
import treams_rs.advect as tr

def scattering(radius):
    sphere = tr.sphere_tmatrix(k0=1.3, lmax=2, radius=radius, material=3.0)
    incident = tr.plane_wave([0, 0, 1], "positive_helicity", k0=1.3)
    return sphere.cross_sections(incident).scattering

value, gradient = ad.value_and_grad(scattering)(np.asarray(0.2))

This is the physics example from frameworks.md:14, using ordinary NumPy only for the input array.

Proposed API after implementation, not current behavior:

import advect as ad
import numpy as np
import treams_rs as tr

def scattering(radius):
    sphere = tr.sphere_tmatrix(k0=1.3, lmax=2, radius=radius, material=3.0)
    incident = tr.plane_wave(
        [0, 0, 1], "positive_helicity", k0=1.3, backend="advect"
    )
    return sphere.cross_sections(incident).scattering

value, gradient = ad.value_and_grad(scattering)(np.asarray(0.2))

The explicit choice on the constant-only wave illustrates the ambiguity honestly. A one-time explicit backend namespace is another smaller option for users wanting completely unchanged objective bodies.

Executed evidence:

  • Two tiny single-thread probes used existing advect: .venv/bin/python -B, with bytecode writes disabled and OMP/OpenBLAS/MKL/NumExpr/Rayon thread limits set to one.
  • Current source imported as Advect 0.3.0. During value_and_grad, is_traced(x) was true; is_traced([x]) false; x.__array_namespace__() is numpy true; np.asarray(x) raised TracingError. NumPy sum(sin(x)**2) at [0.2] produced value 0.039469502998557456, gradient [0.38941834].
  • The treams docs’ old float-to-complex caveat at frameworks.md:289 is explicitly from Advect 0.2.0. It did not reproduce on the inspected current Advect: both Python float and NumPy scalar-array inputs to ad.grad(lambda e: anp.abs(e + 0.1j)**2) returned 6.0.
  • No treams-rs distribution was available in that environment, and the treams checkout had no .venv. I did not execute treams physics examples, install dependencies, rebuild, modify files or Git state, or contact anyone.

advect.is_traced is already a documented public API in both locally available tags:

Tag Commit
v0.2.0 0641bf0fd51f7f8198bd13e515360da4e82be9a1
v0.2.1 9636a04a18b2d53a11f3d832ff467485a64a662b

At both tag revisions:

  • packages/advect/src/advect/__init__.py:31 imports it into advect; line 147 includes it in __all__.
  • packages/advect/src/advect/_array.py:13–32 defines the same shallow, non-coercing predicate used today.
  • docs/api/arrays.md:8–10 describes its intended use; line 24 publishes its reference entry.

Thus using advect.is_traced does not require raising treams-rs’s current advect>=0.2.0,<0.4 minimum or adding a compatibility fallback. Later validation should still cover the supported dependency range because other Advect behavior differs between versions, as the scalar-complex probe demonstrated.

Verified entirely with local git show/git rev-parse; no fetch, ref changes, environment changes, or execution of old versions.
